newsitem.title: FINLAND: Poll shows more Finns switch to favour EMU - agency.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows more Finns switch to favour EMU - agency.

text.p: More Finns were in favour of the country being included in the first wave of countries joining Europe's single currency than were against this, according to a new opinion poll cited by Finnish news agency STT on Monday.
The poll, the first to put pro-EMU Finns ahead of opponents of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union, found 45 percent of those surveyed were for joining EMU in 1999 and 42 percent against, STT said.
It was conducted at the beginning of February by Finnish Gallup among 938 people. @
STT said the poll was commissioned by economic think-tank Taloudellinen Tiedotustoimisto, which has links with the Finnish employers' association.
A survey conducted by polling institute Taloustutkimus Oy published at the weekend still showed 41 percent of Finns opposed to EMU, though support had climbed to 38 percent.
That poll covered 1,993 people between January 7 and February 5, 1997.
